dsh-skin-rotation
Smart skin rotation for DeepSeek Harness — random, sequential, weighted or fixed, with a per-skin po
ol, rotation history and crash-safe config writes. Local-first, recoverable, no extra API.
English | 中文
## What it does
You have four skins installed. You like all of them. You use one of them.
`dsh-skin-rotation` applies **one rotation policy** on every launch of DeepSeek Harness and puts the
controls inside the **Skins** settings page:
| Policy | Behaviour |

| `random` | a different skin each launch, optionally never the last 2 or 3 |
| `sequential` | walks

your order, resuming at the right position after a restart |
| `weighted` | probability by weight p

er skin (weights need not total 100) |
| `fixed` | always one chosen skin — no automatic switching |
Everything about it is inspectable and reversible: which skins are in the pool and why the others ar
e not, what was rotated when and why, and the last successful rotation you can restore with one clic
not, what was rotated when and why, and the last successful rotation you can restore with one click.

### Beyond a random pick
- **A real pool** — every installed skin is reported as `compatible`, `excluded`, `incompatible` or

`unavailable`. Excluding a skin only removes it from rotation; installed files are never touched.
-
**Only loadable skins** — DSH silently refuses a plugin row whose `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer range exc
ludes the running version, so a naive rotation can land on a skin that never starts. This plugin mir

rors that admission check and honours the profile's `compatibility.json` grants.
- **History you can
read** — the last rotations with time, from → to, trigger (`startup` / `manual` / `restore`), mode

and outcome. Failed rotations are recorded as failures; they never enter the "recent" set.
- **Resto

re previous** — one click returns to the most recent successful skin that is still usable.
- **Crash
-safe writes** — a rotation edits two patch layers; a journal makes an interrupted write either fini
sh or roll back on the next boot, and it refuses to overwrite files that changed in ways it cannot e

xplain.
- **Versioned state** — the state file carries a `schemaVersion` and migrates forward, so up
grades do not lose your preferences.

## The card
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Control | What it does |
| **Rotate on launch** | Off means the launch leaves the current skin alone. `Shuffle now` still wor

ks. |
| **Mode** | `random` / `sequential` / `weighted` / `fixed`. In `fixed` you pick the skin; not

hing rotates automatically. |
| **Avoid recent** | Prefers a skin that was not among the last 2 or 3
*successful* rotations. It is a preference, never a blocker: with nowhere fresh to go it still pick

s one and says so. |
| **Skin checkboxes** | Pool membership. Unchecking is an exclusion, not an uni

nstall. Incompatible skins cannot be re-enabled. |
| **Weights** | Shown in `weighted` mode. `0` rem

oves a skin from the draw; an empty box means the default weight `1`. |
| **Restore previous** | Ret
urns to the most recent successful skin that is still in the pool, and records the restore in the hi
the most recent successful skin that is still in the pool, and records the restore in the history. |
A manual switch in the skin manager still wins — until the next launch, which is the entire point.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- **Rotation is a host-side decision, made once per launch.** A process-level boot key means a hot r
eload of the plugin re-runs `apply` without rotating again; a real restart does rotate. A browser re

fresh never re-rolls the dice.
- **It edits the patch layers, not the skins.** The plugin rewrites t
he same `# --- dsh-skin managed ---` block the skin manager owns, in both the profile patch and the
higher-priority home patch. Every line outside that block — hand-written rows, comments, DSH's own a

ppended settings rows — is preserved byte for byte, and writes go through a temp file plus rename.
-
**It only picks skins the host will load.** DSH denies any plugin row whose `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` pee
r range excludes the running version: the patch still says `disabled: false`, the row simply never s
tarts, and you get no skin at all. This plugin mirrors that admission check with its own SemVer rang
e evaluator and honours the profile's `compatibility.json` grants, so a random pick cannot land on a

dead skin.
- **The browser half is one card.** It observes the DOM, appends one container to the sk
in manager's page root, and renders the card into it. It registers no settings page of its own, keep

s no global state, and removes every observer, timer and style tag it created when it unloads.
- **I
t never touches a skin's files, `skin.json`, or the manager's own state.**
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness web profile, `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` (declared as `engines.dsh`).
- At least two
installed skins for rotation to mean anything. Skins are read the way the ecosystem defines them: a

package shipping a valid `skin.json` (`id`, `package`, `bodyAttr`, `wiring.id`).
- The card lives in
side the skin manager's Skins page (`settings.section` id `dsh-skins`). Without that manager rotatio

n still works — you drive it through the route instead of a card.
- No `@deepseek-ai/*` runtime depe

ndency: nothing to resolve, nothing to build, no install-time scripts.
- Windows and POSIX both work

: writes go to a temp file plus rename, and the recovery journal is plain JSON.
- Independently inde
xed by dsh.so: security audit done (low risk), `L5` install verification — run tested on dsh `0.2.0-
dsh.so: security audit done (low risk), `L5` install verification — run tested on dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`.
